metadata.goal: Identify unusual or distinctive service patterns in repeated courier routes and explain how they differ from a straightforward one-stop–one-task process.
metadata.header: Distinctive Service Patterns Across Repeated Courier-Days
metadata.dataset_description: The case contains 97 tasks and six Shanghai road-network trajectories. Availability and completion times allow pending-task exceptions to be inferred without answer-label fields.

insight_list.insight: The courier passes close to a pending task without completing it, leaves the area to serve several other tasks, and returns much later to complete the skipped delivery.

plot.title: Skipped Pending Task Against Prompt-Completion Baseline
plot.description: The exception-day map is paired with first-approach-to-completion delays for all tasks.

insight_list.question: Is there a task that was already available when the courier passed it, but was completed only after a much later return?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare availability time, first close GPS approach, and completion time for every task.
insight_list.code:
import pandas as pd, numpy as np
o=df.copy(); t=user_df.copy()
o["available_time"]=pd.to_datetime(o.available_time); o["completion_time"]=pd.to_datetime(o.completion_time); t["gps_time"]=pd.to_datetime(t.gps_time)
def km(a,b,c,d):
 p1,p2=np.radians(b),np.radians(d);z=np.sin((p2-p1)/2)**2+np.cos(p1)*np.cos(p2)*np.sin(np.radians(c-a)/2)**2;return 6371.0088*2*np.arctan2(np.sqrt(z),np.sqrt(1-z))
rows=[]
for r in o.itertuples():
 q=t[(t.trajectory_id==r.trajectory_id)&(t.gps_time>=r.available_time)&(t.gps_time<=r.completion_time)].copy();q["distance"]=km(q.lng,q.lat,r.task_lng,r.task_lat);close=q[q.distance<=.08];first=close.iloc[0] if len(close) else q.loc[q.distance.idxmin()];rows.append((r.task_id,(r.completion_time-first.gps_time).total_seconds()/60))
print(pd.DataFrame(rows,columns=["task_id","delay_min"]).sort_values("delay_min",ascending=False).head())

insight_list.insight: Several nearby deliveries are completed within a short time interval while the courier’s recorded position changes very little.

plot.title: Rapid Nearby Deliveries Across Courier-Days
plot.description: Six day-level profiles show repeated rapid completions with limited displacement.

insight_list.question: Does rapid completion of nearby tasks recur across independent courier-days?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare elapsed completion time and displacement within each day’s dense local batch.

insight_list.insight: Instead of progressing steadily from one service area to the next, the courier repeatedly returns to previously visited areas, producing a fragmented route with several cross-area transitions.

plot.title: Fragmented Area Transitions Across Courier-Days
plot.description: Completion-area sequences show repeated returns on all six days.

insight_list.question: Do independent courier-days progress steadily across areas, or repeatedly return to areas served earlier?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Inspect ordered service-area sequences and count returns to previously served areas.

insights: The courier passes close to a pending task without completing it, leaves the area to serve several other tasks, and returns much later to complete the skipped delivery.
Several nearby deliveries are completed within a short time interval while the courier’s recorded position changes very little.
Instead of progressing steadily from one service area to the next, the courier repeatedly returns to previously visited areas, producing a fragmented route with several cross-area transitions.
summary: Across six courier-days, rapid local batches and fragmented cross-area returns recur as normal patterns, while one already-available task is uniquely passed and completed only after a much later revisit.
